sections.label: Budget cut for Head X
sections.summary: The speaker moves to reduce Head X of the Estimates by $100, citing core values and post-pandemic discourse on race, social economic status and nationality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head X of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I believe that our core values of building a caring and inclusive, multiracial, multicultural and multi-religious society remain sacrosanct among Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: However, it is undeniable that, as each new generation of Singaporeans come to the fore, we will have to continue to evolve as a society and refresh our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This House will recollect that, emerging from the COVID-19 pandemic last year, we observed a series of highly emotive discourse on issues of race, social economic status and nationality.

sections.label: Unite Pillar and Malay income
sections.summary: The speaker asks Minister Edwin Tong to update on the Unite Pillar and MCCY strategies, and notes Malay household income of $15,000 or more rose from 2.6% in 2010 to 8.5% in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Unite Pillar led by Minister Edwin Tong, in particular, is well placed to tackle these issues head on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to update us on his experience so far as a lead for the Unite Pillar in the Forward Singapore exercise, as well as to share with us MCCY's strategies to ensure that we can create a Singapore, where every citizen belong, is able to maintain strong bonds with one another and is able to contribute collectively to build a strong, inclusive and cohesive society in a country where all of us can proudly call our home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   Our Malay/Muslim community, with the support of all Singaporeans, has become more successful. 8.5% of the Malay population have a monthly household income of $15,000 or more in 2020, compared to 2.6% in 2010, and I am confident that figure will continue to rise.

sentences.text: But rather than crippling us, we have become a role model in managing challenges and diversity as a community and other communities learn and can learn a lot from us, whether it is in setting up self-help groups to improve education outcomes or bringing down drug abuse.

sentences.text: However, it has never been formalised and this initiative we now have undertaken is something that they want to support and they want to develop more of and contribute to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: We are starting on our own first, through the ICCOS.

sections.label: Religious scholars knowledge repository
sections.summary: Religious scholars are undertaking post-graduate studies and contributing to a body of knowledge to be a repository for future religious leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: At the same time, our own religious scholars are now undertaking post-graduate studies as well as contributing to this body of knowledge, through the RPCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: So, we hope that putting this together as a repository, one day, as soon as possible, to have a body of knowledge which we can reference for future leaders, religious leaders, so that we can contribute meaningfully as a minority Muslim community in nation building.

sections.label: Expanding Project Dian towns
sections.summary: The speaker takes final clarifications and is grateful that Project Dian is expanding to more M3@Towns.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Then, I will take a final one or two clarifications on this topic.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: I am grateful that we are now expanding to more	M3@Towns for Project Dian.

sections.label: Project Dian purpose
sections.summary: Project Dian is to help families living in rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Project Dian is to help families living in our rental flats.

sections.label: ECO office and steering committee
sections.summary: An ECO office was set up and a steering committee established with representatives from MSF, SSO, HDB, MOE's UPLIFT programme and M3 agencies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: At the central level, we set up the ECO office, the engagement and coordination office of M3 and we established the steering committee made up of representatives from MSF, SSO, HDB, MOE's UPLIFT programme and the M3 agencies.

sections.label: Reaching pilot town residents
sections.summary: Early efforts in the three pilot towns reached out to 70% of Malay/Muslim residents there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Through the early efforts in the three pilot towns, we have been able to reach out to 70% of our Malay/Muslim residents there.

sections.label: Support for rental flat students
sections.summary: Through MENDAKI, MUIS and MESRA volunteers, students in rental flat families needing educational or socio-emotional support are assessed and channelled resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: The key to it is to access the resources available and through our network of agencies, MENDAKI, MUIS and MESRA, we have a pool of volunteers, so any students in the rental flat families, whether they go to madrasahs or whether they go to our national schools, if they need educational support, if they need socio-emotional support, we will certainly assess the resources available to them and channel resources available to them.

sections.label: Early childhood education resources
sections.summary: Resources should be spent on very young children to enhance early childhood education and support cognitive and social emotional development early.

sentences.speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
sentences.text: Of more concern to us, really, is the very young children, for us to make sure that the resources are spent on them, to be able to enhance their ability for early childhood education so that their cognitive and social emotional development get supported right at a very early age.

sections.label: Support for You Calculator
sections.summary: A retired resident unsure of his benefits was shown with the Support for You Calculator that he could expect $2,800 this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: In fact, when one retired resident was unsure of the benefits he could enjoy, I used the Support for You Calculator and showed him that he could expect $2,800 this year.

sections.label: Government-citizen bonds and participation
sections.summary: The initiatives aim to strengthen Government-citizen bonds and partnerships for citizen participation, and MCCY is asked to share their effectiveness and outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: They aim to strengthen Government-citizen bonds and partnerships for citizen participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask MCCY to share the effectiveness of these initiatives and the key outcomes that have emerged from these exercises.

sections.label: Arts Plan 2.0 objectives
sections.summary: Low Yen Ling shared NAC's consultation on Arts Plan 2.0, a public consultation in second half of 2022, and MCCY's three objectives for the plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling had shared at the time, that the National Arts Council (NAC) was in deep consultation with stakeholders on the Arts Plan 2.0 and that a public consultation will be conducted in the second half of 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: She also shared that MCCY’s objectives for the Arts Plan 2.0 were three-fold: first, to strengthen the role of arts in the wider local and global creative economy; second, to develop further ways for the arts to contribute to deepening our national identity, social cohesion and inclusivity; and third, to make the arts a distinctive factor that adds to Singapore’s attractiveness as a global city.

sections.label: National Monuments gazetting
sections.summary: The Preservation of Monuments Act lets the Government gazette monuments of historic, cultural, traditional, archaeological, architectural, artistic or symbolic significance and national importance as National Monuments, currently 75.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: These are monuments that are of such historic, cultural, traditional, archaeological, architectural, artistic or symbolic significance and national importance that the Preservation of Monuments Act allows the Government to preserve and gazette them as National Monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: We currently have a total of 75 buildings and structures that have been gazetted as National Monuments.

sections.label: Safeguarding built heritage
sections.summary: The speaker says it is imperative to protect and promote collective heritage and invites the Minister to share MCCY's plans to safeguard built heritage, particularly National Monuments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: It is, therefore, imperative that we continue to ensure that we do our utmost to protect and to promote our collective heritage as we build on our social compact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: I, therefore, invite the Minister to share more about MCCY’s plans to safeguard and preserve our built heritage, particularly our National Monuments.

sections.label: Local arts and culture
sections.summary: Promoting local arts and culture is important for strengthening belonging and identity and bridging generations and languages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: What people are most concerned about is: if lives are affected, what will happened to our social harmony and cohesion built over the years under this immense pressure?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Hence, promoting local arts and culture is important in strengthening our sense of belonging and identity, as arts and culture carry our history and shared values, and serve as a bridge across different generations and languages.

sections.label: Chinese dialect decline
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned that few Singaporeans below 50 will be conversant in Chinese dialects in 20 or 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: But many may not speak or speak competently.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I am concerned at this rate there may hardly be some any Singaporeans below 50 who will be conversant in our Chinese dialects in another 20 or 30 years.

sections.label: Dialect learning and broadcast ban
sections.summary: The speaker suggests dialect options at MOE Language Centre and Institutes of Higher Learning and asks if the Government will lift the ban on TV and radio dialect programmes since 1981.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: While our clan associations do offer dialect classes, offering dialects as a third language option at the MOE Language Centre and our Institutes of Higher Learning can be an option to instill interest and promote knowledge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: NUS saw a great demand when they offered dialect modules in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider lifting the general ban on TV and radio dialect programmes which is in place since 1981 which can signal to many Singaporeans who take the cue from the Government?

sections.label: Kallang Alive Precinct announcement
sections.summary: The Kallang Alive Precinct was first announced in 2019 as part of URA's masterplan to rejuvenate the Kallang River.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Kallang Alive Precinct was first announced in 2019 as part of URA’s masterplan to rejuvenate the Kallang River.

sections.label: Sports Hub partnership termination
sections.summary: The Government terminated its public-private partnership with Sports Hub Pte Ltd to integrate Sports Hub operations with other sporting venues in the precinct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The recent decision by the Government to terminate the public-private partnership with Sports Hub Pte Ltd (SHPL) is driven primarily by the need to integrate the operations of Sports Hub more closely with those of other sporting venues within the precinct so that we can achieve the sports and entertainment vibrancy that we have envisioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Chairman, Singapore SG has taken over the management of Sports Hub since last year and can MCCY thus share what are the developments that have occurred since last December and also the future plans of Sports Hub, and how it will feature as part of the Kallang Alive Precinct?

sections.label: Sports Hub and community facilities plans
sections.summary: The speaker asks about the Ministry's plans for Sports Hub programming and infrastructure and for building, refurbishing, upgrading and maintaining community sports facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: What are the Ministry's plans for the Sports Hub this year, in the year ahead, in terms of both programming and infrastructural development as part of its roadmap to unlock the Sports Hub's full potential for Singapore and Singaporeans?

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share what are its plans to build new community sports facilities and to refurbish, upgrade and maintain existing ones so that Singaporeans can look forward to enjoying sports in the community even more conveniently?

sections.label: National School Games at National Stadium
sections.summary: MOE announced last month that the National School Games track and field finals would return to the National Stadium.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just last month, the Ministry of Education (MOE) announced that the National School Games track and field finals would return to the National Stadium.

sections.label: Protecting national training dates
sections.summary: More communication between NSAs, SportSG, KASM and event promoters is proposed to identify critical dates when national training should be protected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The anticipated increase in events at the Sports Hub will inevitably disrupt national training and national teams could potentially be displaced for several days if the facility is used for an event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, it would be good to enable more communication between NSAs, SportSG, KASM and event promoters to identify critical dates when national training should be protected, for instance, the period right before a national games or competition.

sections.label: New sporting projects welcomed
sections.summary: The speaker is encouraged by new sporting projects like Punggol Recreational Sports Centre and Toa Payoh Integrated Development under the Singapore Sports Facilities Masterplan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a National Sports Association President, access to facilities for development and high-performance programmes is always at the forefront of my considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am encouraged by recent announcements of new sporting projects, such as Punggol Recreational Sports Centre and Toa Payoh Integrated Development that are part of the Singapore Sports Facilities Masterplan.

sections.label: Pathways for young football talents
sections.summary: Many pathways exist for young football talents, including ActiveSG Football Academy Development Centre, Unleash The Roar, Singapore Sports School, S-League Youth Teams and private clubs like Lion City Sailors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Chairman, currently, we have many pathways for our young football talents, such as ActiveSG Football Academy Development Centre, Unleash The Roar, Singapore Sports School, S-League Youth Teams under 12, under 14, under 16 national development squads and private clubs like Lion City Sailors.

sections.label: Overseas training and foreign club partnerships
sections.summary: Initiatives such as sending youth teams for overseas training and establishing partnerships with foreign clubs are being considered and/or pursued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Since that time, I understand that the initiatives. such as sending youth teams to overseas training, establishment of partnerships with foreign clubs and other measures are being considered and/or pursued.

sections.label: Developing local players, coaches and clubs
sections.summary: The speaker proposes that FAS and stakeholders hold an open national conversation with local players and coaches, both current and former.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: While I understand the reasons behind recruiting foreign bond players to play for Singapore in the longer term, we need to focus on developing our local players, coaches and clubs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Local players who have dedicated their time playing for Singapore could be employed in various role where their experience could be relevant towards improving our system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Therefore, I propose that the Football Association of Singapore and other relevant stakeholders engage in an open conversation, maybe a national conversation with our local players and coaches, both current and former.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: Notably, in London, Oakland and Singapore, Active Citizens Worldwide (ACW)'s 2018 report indicated that sports and physical activity generate an estimated $454 million in savings annually and results in 19,800 additional years of healthy life and 575 fewer deaths in Singapore.

sections.label: Residents seek sports facilities rejuvenation
sections.summary: Residents have given feedback that several facilities are often under maintenance and want the sports complex, stadium and sports centre rejuvenated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In recent years, residents have feedback to meet that several of the facilities are often under maintenance and express their desire for the sports complex, stadium and sports centre to be rejuvenated.

sections.label: Mandatory mediation and dispute cases
sections.summary: It was announced that noise disputes, post-mediation CMC disputes and CDRT claims must first go through mandatory mediation or parties will be penalised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: At the MinLaw COS debate on 27 February, it was announced that disputes over noise issues, disputes that have resurfaced after mediation at the Community Mediation Centre (CMC), and disputes in which parties want to file a claim with the Community Disputes Resolution Tribunal (CDRT) must first go through mandatory mediation or the parties involved will be penalised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the enhanced CDMF, how will MCCY proceed to assist in the other types of dispute cases not in the above three categories?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: What about cases involving religious practices that might cause racial or religious tensions, persons with mental health or suspected mental health issues?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can MCCY try to expedite the processing of these cases?

sections.label: Updates on outcomes and efforts
sections.summary: MCCY is asked to provide updates on the outcomes and ongoing efforts since then.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can MCCY provide updates on the outcomes and ongoing efforts since then?

sections.label: SG Cares Volunteer Centres work
sections.summary: Since 2018, SG Cares Volunteer Centres have engaged community partners including schools, businesses and SSAs to support beneficiaries and grow volunteers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
sentences.text: Since they were set up in 2018, the SG Cares Volunteer Centres in their respective towns have been engaging and coordinating with community partners including schools, businesses and Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to better support beneficiaries in need but harnessing community resources and growing the pool of volunteers.

sections.label: Medical escort demand and matching
sections.summary: Centres may lack resources, demand for medical escorts is high, volunteers are few, and matching volunteers with patients needs coordinating personnel and IT.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Sometimes, the centres may not have the resources to engage them at the level which they are willing to serve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I understand from most of the SSAs in my constituency that there is a high demand for medical escorts, especially among the elderly, to help vulnerable patients keep their medical appointments at polyclinics and Government hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Volunteers in this area are few, and in most instances, the staff in the SSAs have to handle this work, on top of their own work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The other challenge is matching the volunteers and the patients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We need coordinating personnel and a good IT system to draw up the schedules and match with those of the volunteers, including reserve medical escorts, in case a volunteer, who has been assigned to the senior, is suddenly unable to make it.

sections.label: SG Cares Volunteer Centres partners
sections.summary: Established in 2018, the SG Cares Volunteer Centres have connected with local partners such as schools, businesses and NSAs to support people in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: Chairman, established in 2018, the SG Cares Volunteer Centres has actively connected with local partners, such as schools, businesses and National Sports Associations (NSAs), to support people in need through community resources and volunteers.

sections.label: Forward Singapore exercise discussions
sections.summary: Over 14,000 Singaporeans have discussed what they want for Singapore's future since the Forward Singapore exercise launched.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since the launch of the Forward Singapore exercise, over 14,000 Singaporeans from all walks of life have come together to discuss what we want to see for Singapore's future.

sections.label: MCCY arts and heritage spending
sections.summary: MCCY has spent about $450 million yearly on arts and heritage, with COVID-19 support packages and a 35% rise in NAC-managed arts space from 2010 to 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years or so, MCCY has committed public spending on arts and heritage at about $450 million every year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In addition, during COVID-19, we rolled out the $75 million Arts and Culture and Resilience Package to support our practitioners during the pandemic and injected an additional $12 million to help ensure that our talent is preserved and support the continued transformation of the arts and heritage sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Just taking arts gross floor area (GFA) managed by the National Arts Council (NAC), this has increased by 35% over the period 2010 to 2020, and this excludes other arts spaces which exists in the private and commercial spaces.

sections.label: Consultation on SG Arts and Heritage Plans
sections.summary: NAC and NHB consulted over 2,000 stakeholders on the next edition of Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans over the past 20 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Over the past 20 months, NAC and the National Heritage Board (NHB) have consulted over 2,000 stakeholders on the next edition of Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans.

sections.label: SG Arts Plan creative economy focus
sections.summary: The SG Arts Plan 2023 to 2027 will place greater focus on the Creative Economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For our SG Arts Plan 2023 to 2027, we will place greater focus on the Creative Economy.

sections.label: NAC new focus areas
sections.summary: NAC will look at new focus areas such as intellectual property rights, new business models and digital adoption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: NAC will, thus, be looking at new focus areas, such as intellectual property rights, new business models and digital adoption.

sections.label: University of the Arts student programmes
sections.summary: With the upcoming University of the Arts, students will benefit from existing LASALLE and NAFA programmes and new programmes for the creative economy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In addition, with the upcoming University of the Arts, students will benefit from existing programmes offered by LASALLE and NAFA, as well as new programmes, to meet the needs of the creative economy.

sections.label: Istana main building restoration
sections.summary: Restoration works for the main Istana building are expected to start early next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Restoration works for the main Istana building are expected to commence early next year.

sections.label: Expanding National Collection to designs
sections.summary: The National Collection will be expanded to include designs so Singaporeans can see top-class designers' works.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We have some top-class designers in Singapore among us, and we want Singaporeans to see their works and be proud of their achievements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, expand the National Collection to include designs.

sections.label: Taking over Singapore Sports Hub
sections.summary: Ownership and management of the Singapore Sports Hub were taken over, and Kallang Alive Sport Management Company was set up under Sport Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In this spirit, we took over the ownership and management of the Singapore Sports Hub, to unlock its full potential, to make Sports Hub more accessible to all Singaporeans, and to achieve a deeper integration with the rest of the Kallang Alive Precinct.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We set up Kallang Alive Sport Management Company, or as Mr Mark Chay calls them, in short – and we all love our acronyms – KASM, which operates under the ambit of Sport Singapore.

sections.label: Concerts and upcoming Sports Hub events
sections.summary: Two concerts drew over 50,000 people, with upcoming entertainment and sports events including Harry Styles, Blackpink, Singapore Smash and Rugby Sevens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The two concerts welcomed more than 50,000 people to the Sports Hub.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the coming months, Singaporeans can also look forward to world-renowned entertainment events, such as for those Members who are interested, Harry Styles, Blackpink as well as marquee sports events, such as the World Table Tennis Singapore Smash, happening this week and next, and the HSBC Singapore Rugby Sevens, happening next month.

sections.label: Kallang Alive Precinct developments
sections.summary: Kallang Football Hub and Kallang Tennis Centre in the Kallang Alive Precinct are due to be completed later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The developments in the larger Kallang Alive Precinct, in other words, the areas outside of Sports Hub that can be used to synergise with Sports Hub is also on track, with the Kallang Football Hub, with four sheltered and three unsheltered pitches, and the Kallang Tennis Centre, comprising seven indoor and twelve outdoor courts, due to be completed later this year.

sections.label: Sports Facilities Master Plan and participation
sections.summary: The Sports Hub and Kallang Alive plans are part of the Sports Facilities Master Plan, and regular sports participation rose from 54% in 2015 to 66% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our plans for the Sports Hub and Kallang Alive Precinct are part of a larger Sports Facilities Master Plan (SFMP) to develop and refresh National Training Centres (NTCs) for elite athlete training and sports facilities across Singapore for all Singaporeans to enjoy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Based on our National Sport Participation Survey, residents who participate in sports and exercise regularly at least once a week has risen from 54% in 2015 to 66% in 2019.

sections.label: ActiveSG credits and new sports
sections.summary: Two more sports, Floorball and Volleyball, will be introduced, and citizens and permanent residents aged four to 12 will get $100 in ActiveSG credits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: This year, we plan to introduce two more – Floorball and Volleyball.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Therefore, all Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged four to 12 years old will receive a top-up of $100 worth of ActiveSG credits.

sections.label: School Football Academies established
sections.summary: Since 2021, 12 School Football Academies were established, two of which have dedicated programmes for girls.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Since 2021, we established 12 School Football Academies (SFAs), of which two, have dedicated programmes for girls.

sections.label: National football development centre
sections.summary: A national football development centre will be set up as the main training centre for all national youth squads.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: First, we will set up a national football development centre as the main training centre for all our national youth squads.

sections.label: Inaugural UTR scholarship launch
sections.summary: The inaugural UTR scholarship will be launched later this year, sending young footballers to overseas academies for education and training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Last but certainly not least, we will launch the inaugural UTR scholarship later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Our best young footballers will be sent to overseas academies that offer good quality education alongside the best football training and competitive environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Therefore, through this stint, they will come back with academic qualifications that will allow them to continue future studies at the tertiary level in Singapore or overseas, even as they train and compete with the best amongst the overseas talents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will start this programme later this year and we are considering a good academy in Europe to kick off this programme with.

sections.label: Early enlistment for footballers
sections.summary: Early enlistment is a possibility for footballers with NS obligations after their stint, as explored with Irfan Fandi.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For footballers with NS obligations, in other words, after they return, after they finish their stint, early enlistment is a possibility and one we have explored, quite successfully with several other footballers, for example, with Irfan Fandi.

sections.label: Noise disputes mediation share
sections.summary: In 2022, noise-related disputes were about 65% of neighbour-related disputes registered for mediation at MinLaw's Community Mediation Centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In 2022, noise-related disputes made up about 65% of all neighbour-related disputes registered for mediation at MinLaw's Community Mediation Centre.

sections.label: Expanding mediators and mediation agreements
sections.summary: Mediator pool will be expanded and deployed into the community, and mediation settlement agreements given more standing to encourage compliance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: To support mediation services, we will expand the pool of mediators as well as forward deploy them as far as possible, into the community so, it is not just all centralised at the CMC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will also be giving mediation settlement agreements more teeth and standing, to encourage greater compliance with the mediated outcomes.

sections.label: Preserving neighbour relations, public consultation
sections.summary: It helps preserve and mend relations between neighbours, and residents will be invited to share views in a public consultation on CDMF enhancements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It helps to preserve, and in some cases, even mend and make better the relations between neighbours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will invite residents to share their views on this when we conduct the public consultation on the proposed CDMF enhancements later this year.

sections.label: Expanding programme to Secondary 4 students
sections.summary: From 2023, the programme will be expanded to nominated Secondary 4 students from all MOE schools and madrasahs in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: From 2023, we will expand the programme to nominated Secondary 4 students from all MOE schools and madrasahs in Singapore.

sections.label: Expanding SG Cares Volunteer Centres
sections.summary: Individuals and corporates are encouraged to play a more active role, and SG Cares Volunteer Centres' capabilities will be expanded and deepened.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Beyond youths, we are encouraging individuals and corporates to play an even more active role to come together, work for the social good, leverage on corporate purpose and uplift our communities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We will therefore expand and deepen the capabilities of our SG Cares Volunteer Centres.

sections.label: SHG youth dialogues and volunteering
sections.summary: SHGs will launch inter-SHG Youth Dialogues on Forward Singapore themes and create more cross-SHG volunteering opportunities open to all ethnic groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: For example, the SHGs will launch a series of inter-SHG Youth Dialogues centring around themes emerging from the ongoing Forward Singapore exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: These dialogues will bring together young people from different backgrounds and different ethnicities and empower them to develop and lead ground-up solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: The SHGs will also create more opportunities for volunteers to interact, to serve with one another across the different SHGs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: We do not have volunteers from an SHG that come from only a particular group that the SHG serves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: It is open and we encourage all volunteers to come, from a broad spectrum of different ethnic groups to serve the broader spectrum of society through the SHGs.

sections.label: MCCY building social compact
sections.summary: MCCY will work with all Singaporeans to build an enduring social compact where people stand and act as one united people.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: On our part, MCCY will continue to work with all Singaporeans, join our strengths and inspire a collective action to build an enduring social compact where we stand and act as one united people, and we are proud to call Singapore our home.

sections.label: Children's Museum and arts initiatives
sections.summary: The Children's Museum Singapore opened last year, and MCCY is asked about other initiatives and collaborations with MOE and Made for Families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: The Children's Museum Singapore, being the first ever Museum dedicated to children in Singapore was opened last year, aspiring to be a place of Wonder and joy for our little ones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Apart from Children's Museum, what other initiatives is MCCY looking into, to create additional opportunities for our young ones to understand our arts and heritage through play and learning experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Is MCCY working with MOE and PMO's Made for Families to explore more collaborations with a view to inspire more of our children to pursue arts as their passion, as well as deepen their knowledge of Singapore's tradition, traditional heritage and culture, and at the same time, encourage more family-bonding opportunities?

sections.label: Technology and arts practitioners
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Government has helped arts and cultural practitioners make a living or breakthroughs in the past year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: If we can better use technologies, we will be able to expand our reach and grasp new opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask how the Government has helped arts and cultural practitioners continue to make a living or even make breakthroughs in the past year.

sections.label: SG Arts Plan and stART Fund
sections.summary: The SG Arts Plan launched in 2018, and the Sustain the Arts Fund benefited 22 small arts organisations in the last financial year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Our SG Arts Plan, which was first launched in year 2018, has since inspired Singaporeans from all walks of life, connected communities and reflected our unique Singapore identity to the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We launched the Sustain the Arts Fund, in short called stART, to encourage giving to small arts organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The fund has benefited 22 small art organisations just in the last financial year, including Reverberance, which is a Chinese wind-percussion ensemble that seeks to inspire the community through traditional arts.

sections.label: Refreshing arts master plan
sections.summary: Five years on, the arts master plan is being refreshed to respond to challenges of a post-COVID-19 environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Five years on, our arts master plan is being refreshed to respond to the challenges of a post-COVID-19 environment.

sections.label: NAC arts infrastructure study
sections.summary: NAC has embarked on a study to map out existing arts infrastructure in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To this end, NAC has embarked on a study to map out existing arts infrastructure in Singapore.

sections.label: Heritage Plan 2023 to 2027
sections.summary: The Heritage Plan for 2023 to 2027 will focus on enhancing Singapore's legacy in identity, community, industry and innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, I am happy to announce that our Heritage Plan for year 2023 to 2027 will focus on enhancing our Singapore legacy in four key areas – identity, community, industry and innovation.

sections.label: Expanding National Collection to design
sections.summary: The National Collection will be expanded to cover the realm of design, as mentioned by Minister Edwin Tong.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In addition, we will expand the National Collection to cover the realm of design, as mentioned by Minister Edwin Tong.

sections.label: Growing Singapore heritage industry
sections.summary: Initiatives will share Singapore's story with regional and global audiences, and the Organisation Transformation Grant will strengthen the heritage sector's sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: To grow our heritage industry, we will share our rich Singapore story with a wider regional and global audience through a range of initiatives, like forming new platforms to showcase our traditional crafts and highlighting our culture and heritage overseas.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: We will also continue to strengthen the sustainability of our heritage sector through the ongoing Organisation Transformation Grant (OTG), which encourages heritage businesses to adopt innovative projects.

sections.label: Arts metaverse alliance for action
sections.summary: NAC will establish the Alliance for Action for Project Arts Metaverse this year to co-create digital solutions with stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: As technology continues to permeate our lives and artistic expressions, the rise of the metaverse will open up new doors of opportunities for our arts and culture sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I am glad to announce that NAC will establish the Alliance for Action for Project Arts Metaverse this year to partner and co-create digital solutions with our stakeholders for this new world of possibilities.

sections.label: Competency Frameworks for arts practitioners
sections.summary: NAC is developing Competency Frameworks, starting with arts education, technical theatre and production, to be launched later this year with roadshows.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: Since last year, NAC has been working closely with the sector on the competencies needed for the arts practitioners to grow in their career.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: I am glad to share that NAC is developing Competency Frameworks to help practitioners hone their skills, starting with one for those in arts education, technical theatre and production.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: This framework, which will be launched later this year, will be accompanied by roadshows to guide practitioners on the recommended skillsets.

sections.label: Reviewing Arts Resource Hub
sections.summary: The Arts Resource Hub, formed in 2019, has over 2,500 subscribers and close to 76 talks and workshops, and NAC is reviewing it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The Arts Resource Hub (ARH), which was formed in 2019 to support the SEP community, has since gained over 2,500 subscribers and held close to 76 talks and workshops.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: NAC is currently reviewing the ARH to better support the needs of SEPs.

sections.label: Somerset Belt youth precinct masterplan
sections.summary: The Somerset Belt aims to be a vibrant youth precinct, and a Masterplan was put up in 2020 after engagement sessions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: It aims to be a vibrant youth precinct to build youth identity and to support their aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
sentences.text: I had the privilege to co-lead the Somerset Belt Working Panel and the team worked with various stakeholders and held many engagement sessions to put up a Somerset Belt Masterplan in 2020.

sections.label: Racial and Religious Harmony progress
sections.summary: The Racial and Religious Harmony was renamed in 2022 with a vision to create networks of trust uniting people regardless of race or religion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh
sentences.text: Since the Racial and Religious Harmony was renamed in 2022, with the vision to create networks of trust that unite people regardless of race or religion, what has been the progress thus far in establishing cooperation, harmony, respect and trust in the community?

sections.label: OBS programming and Coney Island campus
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to share plans for OBS programming and for the new OBS campus on Coney Island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share its plans for OBS programming, going forward, as well as plans for the new OBS campus on Coney Island?

sections.label: Harmony Circles outreach plans
sections.summary: MCCY is asked for an update on its plans for the Harmony Circles and how it will expand outreach to more communities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
sentences.text: Can MCCY provide an update on its plans for the Harmony Circles and how it would ensure that it would be able to expand its outreach to reach more communities?

sections.label: Business and IPC Partnership Scheme
sections.summary: The Business and Institution of a Public Character Partnership Scheme was introduced in 2016 to encourage tax deductions on qualifying expenditures for businesses giving back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: The Business and Institution of a Public Character Partnership Scheme (BIPS) was introduced in 2016 to encourage tax deductions on qualifying expenditures for businesses that give back through volunteerism and service provision.

sections.label: BIPS awareness and application issues
sections.summary: BIPS was introduced in 2016 to encourage employee volunteerism, but many towkays and SMEs are unfamiliar with it and some find the application process tedious.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: In 2016, BIPS was introduced to further encourage employee volunteerism and to foster a culture where businesses and employees support social needs and build a caring and cohesive society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: Majority of the towkays and SMEs I speak with, are unfamiliar with the programme, even though they have extensive corporate responsibility programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
sentences.text: In addition, those who know of the programme, shared that the application process can be tedious, causing both the SSA and the company to give up on the application halfway.

sections.label: SG Mental Well-being Network launch
sections.summary: The Singapore Mental Well-being Network was launched in July to destigmatise, raise awareness of and drive partnerships on mental health and mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Please let me start with mental health and mental well-being.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We launched our Singapore (SG) Mental Well-being Network in July, to destigmatise, raise awareness of and drive partnerships on mental health and mental well-being.

sections.label: Youth mental health and well-being circles
sections.summary: The Network funds and mentors 20 youth teams on mental health with HPB and NYC, and has set up six Mental Well-being Circles.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Third, the Network is working with our Health Promotion Board (HPB) and National Youth Council (NYC) to fund and mentor 20 youth teams to tackle mental health issues in Season 4 of our NYC's Youth Action Challenge.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Fourth, the Network has set up six Mental Well-being Circles across Singapore.

sections.label: Volunteer and beneficiary growth
sections.summary: In the past year, the total number of volunteers and beneficiaries grew by 67% and 50% respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In the past year, the total number of volunteers and beneficiaries grew by 67% and 50% respectively.

sections.label: Corporate Purpose Framework and Blueprint
sections.summary: NVPC and the Singapore Business Federation Foundation launched the Corporate Purpose Framework and Blueprint, with 47 organisations committed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Mr Edward Chia, Mr Mark Chay, Mr Xie Yao Quan and Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked how we are encouraging more businesses to get involved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This January, National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) and the Singapore Business Federation Foundation launched the Corporate Purpose Framework and Blueprint.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This blueprint serves as a common guide for businesses to implement and track their progress in becoming a force for good in society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Thus far, 47 organisations have committed to our blueprint.

sections.label: Mentoring SG mentors and partners
sections.summary: Mentoring SG gathered over 1,000 mentors and 13 corporate partners to create over 4,000 mentoring opportunities, and a Mentoring SG Office is being set up.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Mentoring SG has gathered more than 1,000 mentors and 13 corporate partners, like Micron and DBS, to create over 4,000 mentoring opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We are setting up the Mentoring SG Office to drive this work by growing expertise, resources, and mentoring opportunities at the national level.

sections.label: MOE-OBS Challenge programme resumed
sections.summary: The five-day residential format of the MOE-OBS Challenge programme for Secondary 3 students resumed in January this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about our plans for OBS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We have resumed the five-day residential format of the MOE-OBS Challenge (MOC) programme for Secondary 3 students since January this year.

sections.label: New OBS campus on Coney Island
sections.summary: Construction of the new OBS campus on Coney Island is expected to be completed by 2024, and the Outdoor Adventure Education Council was set up in September.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: They enjoyed making new friends and overcoming challenges together as a team.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: We expect current construction works for our new OBS campus on Coney Island to be completed by 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: This new eco-friendly campus will provide enhanced outdoor activities for our youths, particularly through the MOC programme, which aims to serve our entire cohort of 40,000 Secondary 3 students annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: As we resume OAE for our youths in their formative years, these spaces must provide a safe and enabling environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: That is why we set up the Outdoor Adventure Education Council in September.

sections.label: MCCY athlete support plans
sections.summary: MCCY is asked what plans, provisions and resources it has made for athletes preparing for qualifying events and games, and for emotional and psychological support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: Singapore is gearing up for the 2024 Paris Olympics and Paralympics, but what plans has MCCY made to ensure that our athletes are well-prepared for qualifying events or other events such as the Southeast Asian Games, ASEAN Para Games, Asian Games and Asian Para Games this year?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: What provisions have been made to ensure that aspiring national athletes have been given adequate emotional and psychological support?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: What resources is MCCY providing to these groups to allow them to do their best work?

sections.label: Sports facilities for PwDs, elderly
sections.summary: MCCY is asked for updates on how PwDs and the elderly feature in new sports centre construction and restoration plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: Accessing sports facilities is vital in advancing the health and well-being of society and providing an avenue for social interaction through team sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Chay
sentences.text: Therefore, I am requesting MCCY to give updates on how PwDs and the elderly feature in considerations pertaining to the construction of new sports centres and plans to restore existing ones.

sections.label: Singapore Sports Hall of Fame
sections.summary: The Singapore Sports Hall of Fame was set up in 1985, its induction criteria were reviewed in 2003, and it has 57 inductees to date.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: The Singapore Sports Hall of Fame was set up in 1985 with 24 inductees to honour our top sportsmen and sportswomen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: A review of the induction criteria was conducted in 2003 and a critical change was made – except for Olympics and Paralympics medallists, all other athletes must have served another eight years in any sporting capacity on a national level from the time of them winning a qualifying medal to the time of their induction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: The change in induction criterion resulted in a 12-year gap between the last inductee in 2003 and the next inductee in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: To date, based on the data provided by teamsingapore.sg, there are 57 inductees in the Singapore Sports Hall of Fame.

sections.label: Inclusive ActiveSG facilities progress
sections.summary: SportSG has retrofitted six ActiveSG swimming pools with wheelchair ramps and set up eight inclusive gyms, targeting all 27 gyms by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To date, SportSG has retrofitted swimming pools in six ActiveSG centres with ramps for wheelchairs and has set up eight inclusive ActiveSG gyms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We are on track to make all 27 gyms inclusive by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Through SFMP, residents in Jurong will have greater access to sporting facilities when the ActiveSG Sport Village @ Jurong Town opens in the first half of 2023.

sections.label: National Registry of Exercise Professionals
sections.summary: The National Registry of Exercise Professionals will be launched in three phases to help professionalise the sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To help professionalise the sector, we will launch the National Registry of Exercise Professionals (NREP) in three phases.

sections.label: Sport Leaders Hall of Fame category
sections.summary: A new Sport Leaders category will be added to the Singapore Sport Hall of Fame, with the President giving out awards from this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To honour such individuals who have made extraordinary contributions over a significant period of time, we will include a new category for Sport Leaders in the Singapore Sport Hall of Fame.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: And to elevate the Singapore Sport Hall of Fame as the sporting-equivalent of our Cultural Medallion, I am also pleased to announce that our President will give out the awards starting from this year.

sections.label: DSMP and PwD participation rate
sections.summary: DSMP, launched in 2016, contributed to a rise in sport participation among Persons with Disabilities from 28% in 2015 to 50% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Launched in 2016, DSMP has contributed to increased sport participation rate among Persons with Disabilities (PwDs), with the participation rate rising from 28% in 2015 to 50% in 2019.

sections.label: Coaches upskilled in disability sports
sections.summary: Sport Singapore worked with Republic Polytechnic on Continuing Education and Training courses to upskill over 200 coaches in disability sports coaching since June 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Sport Singapore has also worked with the Republic Polytechnic on Continuing Education and Training courses to upskill more than 200 coaches in disability sports coaching since June 2020.

sections.label: Aloysius ranking and DSMP update
sections.summary: Aloysius beat higher-ranked players at the Boccia World Cup and now ranks 18, as DSMP is reviewed and updated toward a 70% participation target.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: During the Boccia World Cup in November last year, Aloysius also beat more experienced players who were ranked fifth and eighth in the world to advance to the quarter finals.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: So, merely over a year after his international debut, Aloysius ranks 18 in the world now.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With the recent launch of the Enabling Masterplan 2030, it is timely that we review the outcomes of our DSMP initiatives and update our strategies to better support PwDs in sports participation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: By updating the DSMP and with the support of all our stakeholders, we will work towards our 70% target for sport participation amongst PwDs under the Enabling Masterplan 2030.

sections.label: DSMP opportunities for PwDs
sections.summary: The Disabilities Sports Master Plan launched in 2016 has given many PwDs more opportunities to participate in sports and cultivate an active lifestyle.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Disabilities Sports Master Plan (DSMP) launched in 2016 has given many PwDs more opportunities to participate in sports and cultivate an active lifestyle.

sections.label: SG Cares VCs matching volunteers
sections.summary: SG Cares Volunteer Centres work with partners to match volunteers with patients, coordinate training and deployment, and will receive digital tools like the Volunteer Management System.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: On the medical escort initiative that I spoke about just now in my speech, can Minister of State share how the VCs are working to match the patients with the volunteers and how is MCCY strengthening the VCs to help them in this job to do well?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: So, in this regard, the SG Cares VCs, I mentioned earlier on, they work very closely with a multitude of partners, including the social service agencies, social service officers, Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), nursing homes and so on to help to match volunteers with patients, for example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: What the SG Volunteer Centres do then is to coordinate both the training and deployment of relevant volunteers with the requisite skillsets and then match them with the beneficiaries that are also registered with the SG Cares Volunteer Centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I also wanted to say that we will then provide the SG Cares Volunteer Centres with digital tools, such as the Volunteer Management System so that they can better match volunteers as well as beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: There is an upcoming SG Cares Digital Kampong to help to improve the deployment of volunteers through ground needs.

sections.label: National Development Centre and youth teams
sections.summary: Pipelines feed into the National Development Centre, squads come together for competitive matches, and over time national age group international teams will form.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: And when will we launch this development centre?

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We intend to have a broad number of pipelines, all feeding into the National Development Centre (NDC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But on occasion, we bring the squads together, I mentioned that earlier, so that they get to know one another, their playing styles, how they work together as a team, be further developed and enhanced, play competitive matches during the international FIFA seasons, so that they can have the ability to experience competitive matches as a cohort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And over time, this will become our national age group international teams – so under 13, under 15 and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To answer Mr Sharael Taha's question, they remain with the clubs where there will be primary training, or they remain with the SFA at which they compete on a regular basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I mentioned earlier also in my speech that we intend to set up the youth leagues, perhaps in the coming year or two, so that on a regular basis, the clubs will have a regular active competition at a high level so that they can play at that level, week in, week out, then on occasion, come together with the NDC.

sections.label: Creative economy, audience, technology focus
sections.summary: It states three emphases: a creative economy, greater audience centricity, and technology and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
sentences.text: Broadly speaking: number one, there is greater focus on a creative economy; two, greater audience centricity; and the third is the emphasis on technology and innovation.

sections.label: Talent ID in disability space
sections.summary: It says the utmost priority is popularising mainstream or able-bodied talent ID in the disability space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Regarding focus, the Member was also himself a para coach, so I am certain he would know that, in the landscape now, what is probably the utmost priority is to make sure that what is available in the mainstream or able-bodied space of talent ID is popularised in the disability space.

sections.label: Heritage locations Toa Payoh Queenstown
sections.summary: It states that on heritage, the locations discussed are Toa Payoh and Queenstown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: On heritage, definitely, because the locations we are talking about are Toa Payoh, Queenstown.

sections.label: Standardisation of exercise professionals
sections.summary: It states the intent is broad standardisation and accreditation across all exercise professionals in the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: On the professionalisation of exercise professionals, I think our intent is to make sure that there is a broad standardisation and there is a broad sense of accreditation across all exercise professionals in the industry.

sections.label: NDC commencement date July
sections.summary: It states the NDCs are intended to start this year, with an indicative date of July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I did not manage to answer one of Mr Sharael Taha's questions, which was when the NDCs would commence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We intend to start the NDCs by this year and the indicative date is July this year.

sections.label: Early enlistment and athlete development
sections.summary: It states early enlistment, where available, is typically preferable to athletes' development, citing data points and athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That is a paramount obligation and we have to ensure that we work within this framework to ensure that, at the same time, we look at the National Service as a framework but how do we navigate within that system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have found actually, in our own experience and we have collected several data points, it is not just for footballers but athletes as a whole, that typically, an early enlistment where available, is preferable to the athletes' development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: If you enlist early, sometimes at the age of seventeen-and-a-half, close to 18, about 21 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: By the time someone is 19 plus, before 20, he would likely be out there competing and the runway can then be uninterrupted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We had many athletes, in table tennis, Loh Kean Yew was one example as well.
